key_insight: ULTRA unifies multimodal inputs (vision, language, proprioception) into a single control policy that generates autonomous whole-body loco-manipulation behaviors from perception and high-level instructions, removing dependence on tracking predefined motion references.
problem_solved: Overcomes limited/low-quality retargeted data, poor scalability to large skill repertoires, and the common reliance on motion-reference tracking by enabling perception-driven, task-conditioned whole-body control for humanoid robots.
method: A single multimodal control policy that conditions whole-body torque/command outputs on vision, language, and proprioceptive inputs to produce integrated locomotion and manipulation.
Training on heterogeneous and retargeted demonstrations with robustness techniques (data augmentation, weighting/curation) to scale to large skill repertoires despite variable data quality.
Behavior synthesis and task-conditioning (rather than reference tracking) so the robot generates goal-directed, flexible motions from perception and high-level task specs.
impact: Makes humanoid robots more autonomous and practically useful by enabling scalable, perceptual, task-driven loco-manipulation. For ML/robotics practitioners, ULTRA demonstrates how unified multimodal policies and robust dataset strategies can replace brittle reference-following pipelines.

paper_authors: Xialin He, Sirui Xu, Xinyao Li, Runpei Dong, Liuyu Bian
